summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins served front-end work and design ideation on the techworx and orin-dx sites by auditing ~810 past sessions, then act on the findings: add non-binding exploration modes, enforce gate output with a hook, and reduce context-window waste.
summary.outcome: Audit confirmed the plugins were too rigid for exploratory work and had no visual or ideation support. Exploration modes (ADR 011) and a SubagentHandback validation hook with retry cap (ADR 012) were built and committed locally. A context-composition metric and a context-hygiene reference for the smith skills were also added, with the final commit still pending.

repo: Plugins form a spec-driven lifecycle (weaver, vanguard, scribe/muse, navigator, smith, courier) with typed JSON handoffs in shared/schemas and default-fail gates. None has browser, screenshot, visual or generative capability.
spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout, breakpoints or visuals, so a spec can pass muse's exit-gate while saying nothing about appearance.
Muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that was never implemented.
The orin-dx and pages project dirs hold only a few real sessions; the other hundreds of files are subagent transcripts.
Gate loops were churn-heavy: 51 muse:exit-gate calls across 8 specs, every spec failing its first gate, and the 3-retry cap not enforced by the orchestrator.

Validator now lives at shared/hooks/validate-handback.py, reachable by installed plugins through the shared symlink. It is registered via plugins/{muse,scribe,smith,sentinel,ranger}/hooks/hooks.json with matcher SubagentHandback.
A test requires every plugins/*/agents/exit-gate.md to have a ROUTES entry and the plugin to register the hook.

Context measurement: Bash is about 60% of conversation characters (output plus inline script text), and the largest single results are whole-page Artifact reads of 50-56k characters. Delegation prompts are only 3%.
Skill reference files are routed from skills and agents and mirrored to harnesses/codex via `just marketplace-sync`; `just check` is the validation gate.

code.finding: Added RETRY_CAP=3, an escalation_required blocker rule, and WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE JSONL tracing. A retry_count above the cap is accepted only as a fail carrying an escalation_required blocker.
New `context` subcommand attributes characters to user text, assistant text, tool calls, delegation prompts and tool results by tool, and lists the largest results.

New context-hygiene reference covering filtered command output, writing long scripts to files, and reading artifacts by path. It is routed from smith implement, spike, implementer and the Codex counterparts.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output and should be treated as unverified. One early corpus-size assumption (~140 sessions) was corrected by a subagent.
Smoke pilots found skills cannot read schema files when the shared symlink dangles, so record shapes were inlined.
The sandbox blocks GPG signing and writes under ~/.claude/jobs, so commits run with the sandbox disabled (user approved) and scripts go to $TMPDIR.
Compound shell commands containing git add/commit were sometimes refused, so splitting them into separate steps worked.
Measure before cutting: the earlier 77% Bash figure covered results only and understated the real share until command text was included.
Ideation worked best when rendered options were shown and the user answered with short codes; text-first descriptions made the user repeatedly ask 'show me'.

friction: Specs for eight components took ~75 minutes and ~110 agent calls before any visual existed, and the user could not judge them without drawings.
Gate blockers were largely wording or citation residue, and the gate was not monotonic.
Large 60-130 KB spec and plan files stalled agent streams.
Decisions were lost across sessions, frustrating the user.
Visual defects (NavSheet not full screen, translucency, toggle size) were caught only by the user's eye, not by gates.
Sandbox restrictions (GPG, job directory writes, refused compound git commands) forced workarounds.
The first combined add+commit command was refused, requiring retries as separate steps.
open_items: Wave 2 gate hygiene (WP-50-58): evidence-citing blockers, wording-only blockers downgraded to notes, readback, orchestrator-owned spawning. Needs user decision.
Waves 3-5: spec@2, render-evidence, workspace-manifest@2, critic agents, ablations, Codex wording.
Wave 0 leftovers: fixtures, instruction-file linter, plugin-eval suite, wiring paired-analysis into mason.
Exploration gaps: anti-slop controls, tested board generator, cross-session decision retrieval, scratch-only write-guard hook.
Hook live runs for scribe, smith, sentinel and ranger; Codex and Antigravity enforcement equivalents.
Extend the context-hygiene rule to ranger, sentinel, muse and scribe skills after measuring the smith effect.
Port the description-weight cuts from the review-slop branch.
Move exploration record shapes out of skill bodies, then re-pilot.
User review of ADR 011 and ADR 012; recommended accepting ADR 011 and running a paired comparison on a real design task.
Nothing is pushed; the user has not authorized a push or draft PR.
The final context-hygiene commit was issued but its result is unconfirmed.
